request.spec:
A steward can archive the sheet (a button; SHEET_ARCHIVED; anyone else is refused with an error
on the sheet). Show archived yes/no. On an archived sheet everything stays visible and every
change is refused with its usual error, including changing the sheet's today, every bulk action,

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can archive the sheet (a button; SHEET_ARCHIVED; anyone else is refused with an error
on the sheet). Show archived yes/no. On an archived sheet everything stays visible and every
change is refused with its usual error, including changing the sheet's today, every bulk action,

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now archive a sheet. Once it's archived, every change to it is refused with that form's usual error, and everything stays visible. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests (the archive test and the three other scenarios).

**What it does**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V43__sheet_archived.sql`, adds an `archived` flag to the sheet, off by default.
- **Archiving:** a new `POST /api/sheets/{id}/archive` endpoint (`ArchiveSheet.java`). Only someone acting as a steward can use it, and that includes a user the steward role has been delegated to. Anyone else is refused, and so is archiving a sheet that is already archived. A successful archive writes `SHEET_ARCHIVED sheet=<id> by=<user>` to the audit file.
- **Refusing changes:** I added the archived check to `RefuseViewer`, the guard every changing endpoint already runs first. That covers the sheet's today, the paste box, quick-add, people, claims, rates, settings, periods, roles and delegations. The two bulk actions don't use that guard, so the check also sits in the shared claim-status code (`ClaimStatusChange`). On an archived sheet every claim in a bulk action is counted as refused (for example `opened: 0, refused: 1`), and nothing is written.
- **Screen:** the sheet's "today" bar now shows `sheet-archived` (yes/no) and has a `sheet-archive` button. The today form and the archive button share one `sheet-error` element. The test helper doesn't work reliably when two elements with that id are on screen at once.

**Decision for you:** watching a person still works on an archived sheet. It has never been guarded the way sheet changes are, since viewers can do it too, so I treated it as a personal preference rather than a change to the sheet. If you want "every change" to include it, it's a one-line guard in its endpoint file (`watch.POST.yml`).
